A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SALAAD research, with matching methods and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SALAAD pretraining results, compression experiments, hyperparameter ablations and analyses of embedding layers and RPCA decompositions, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds downstream benchmark evaluations, measured training overhead, LM-head experiments and an ADMM update-frequency study.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the coupled loss, adaptive I-controller, penalty scaling and HPA truncation procedure are unchanged. The pipeline diagrams and HPA remark explain existing operations. The newly explicit default exclusion of the LM head does not establish a change from the earlier implementation.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained C4 language-modeling evaluation, v3 Section 5.2 adds actual evaluations on MMLU, ARC-C, COPA, HellaSwag, BoolQ and PIQA. These substantially broaden coverage to knowledge, question answering, reading comprehension and several commonsense reasoning tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains full-rank training, LoRA, ReLoRA, GaLore, LORO, CoLA, SLTrain and LOST. No comparator is added or removed in a matched experiment. The new downstream comparison reuses the existing vanilla baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces zero-shot accuracy evaluation using default lm-evaluation-harness configurations for the 1B models and the 646M compressed variant. Additional protocols include component-wise timing on eight H100 GPUs, a 60M LM-head penalty comparison, and a controlled 1B study of K/J = 5, 10 and 20 with J = 1. Existing pretraining settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds direct evidence on whether LM-head structure can be induced without harming training loss. Appendix I.2 tests how ADMM frequency affects convergence, reconstruction error and block structure. Figure 2 adds measured runtime decomposition beyond v1's analytical cost discussion. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence; the earlier embedding, precision and structural-hyperparameter studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A's average rank and sparsity values with plus/minus summaries are unchanged. v3 introduces no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added performance results are point estimates and trajectories.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. In v3 Table 2, the compressed model scores 36% on HellaSwag and 52% on BoolQ, versus 34% and 55% for vanilla. Appendix I.2 reports final losses of 2.84, 2.84 and 2.78 and reconstruction errors of 10.16, 7.74 and 5.73 for K/J = 5, 10 and 20. Timing and LM-head findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(9), Definition 4.1, the optimization assumptions and computational-cost reasoning are retained. Remark 4.2 clarifies the existing proportional HPA rule and its preservation of learned heterogeneity; it does not introduce a new mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about architecture-preserving SLR induction, adaptive control, elastic deployment and embedding/LM-head asymmetry. The latter was already claimed in v1; its new experiment strengthens support without changing the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the downstream results as evidence against abnormal task-performance collapse, explains update frequency through a regularization-versus-loss trade-off, and expands the rationale for excluding the LM head by default. These refine practical applicability and mechanisms while retaining the earlier central interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, identifies the downstream evaluation harness and default configurations, and specifies eight H100 80GB GPUs for timing. It also clarifies controller calibration and default LM-head exclusion. These are useful disclosures, without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gao et al. (2021) for lm-evaluation-harness. The MatFormer author/venue update refers to the same previously cited work, and the substantive positioning against structured pretraining and elastic inference methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision adds localized method explanations, Remark 4.2, a downstream-evaluation subsection, pipeline and LM-head appendix sections, and a subdivision of the additional ablations. Affiliations and acknowledgements also change. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with training and deployment schematics (Figures 7-8), a runtime breakdown (Figure 2), LM-head and update-frequency plots (Figures 12-13), and downstream and block-statistics tables (Tables 2 and 10). Existing figures and tables are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 supported deployment quality mainly through perplexity and discussed costs analytically, while asserting LM-head asymmetry without a dedicated diagnostic. v3 addresses these important evidence gaps through six-task downstream evaluation, measured training overhead and direct LM-head experiments, alongside a controlled update-frequency analysis. This substantially strengthens the practical assessment and support for the paper's contributions. The added results still lack repeated-run uncertainty and do not establish deployment latency, but those limits do not outweigh the evidential gains.
